transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I haven’t been able to let go of something that’s been going on for almost two years. After a commission I did, I became certain that a few people in the ensemble were quietly trying to undermine my work. It’s things like sudden schedule changes, where people are seated, little comments during rehearsals.

They’ll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it, but it still feels like there’s something else behind it. It’s been hard to shake.
Do you believe it is definitely true that these people are trying to undermine you, even when others show you evidence that points to another explanation?

Yes. I know other people say the emails or notes explain it, and I can see what they’re showing me. But it still doesn’t feel like the real reason.

To me, it seems pretty clear that after that commission, a few people in the ensemble started doing things—changing schedules, placing people a certain way, making small comments in rehearsal—to quietly undermine what I was doing. I’ve tried to talk myself out of it, but I haven’t been able to shake that.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people could not?
No, not really. I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people couldn’t see. It’s more about how I’m interpreting what’s happening around me.
Do you believe these people are deliberately trying to harm you or conspire against you?

I don’t think they’re trying to physically harm me or anything like that. But yes, I do think a few of them have been deliberately working against me.

It’s been going on since that commission — the schedule changes, seating decisions, little comments in rehearsal. Even when they show me emails or notes that explain it, I still feel like there’s another reason behind it, like they’re trying to quietly undermine my work.
Before this started, did you generally tend to distrust other people's motives?

I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve always been careful with people, especially in professional settings, but I wouldn’t say I generally distrusted everyone’s motives before this. This feels more specific to what happened with those people.
Aside from this belief about the ensemble, have you had any other unusual beliefs that other people said were not true?

No, not really aside from that. It’s mainly this one thing with the ensemble. Since the commission, I just can’t shake the feeling—really the certainty—that a few of them have been using schedule changes, seating decisions, and small comments in rehearsals to undermine me.  

Other people keep saying there are normal explanations, and they’ll show me emails or notes, but it still feels like that’s not the real reason.
Has this belief caused a major decline in your work or day-to-day functioning?

Not a major decline, no. It’s affected me, but I’m still getting my work done. I meet deadlines, I’m still composing, and I run most mornings like usual.

Things at home with my wife are basically steady too. So outside of this issue with the ensemble, I’m functioning pretty normally.
Have you had times when your behavior became so disorganized or unusual that other people were concerned or thought you were acting strangely?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been upset and probably more tense in some conversations, but I haven’t had anything where I was acting out of control or so strangely that people were worried in that way.
During this period, have you had a time when you felt unusually high or unusually depressed for days at a time?
No, I don’t think so. I’ve been stressed and preoccupied with all of this, but I haven’t had days where I felt unusually high or really depressed in a way that stood out.
Is it possible, even a little, that you might be mistaken about these people trying to undermine you?

I mean… I understand why you’re asking. But no, not really. I’ve tried to consider that, especially when they show me emails or notes that supposedly explain the schedule changes or seating decisions.

But it’s been almost two years, and the pattern still feels clear to me. After that commission, certain people in the ensemble started making these little moves—changes, comments in rehearsal—that seem meant to undermine my work quietly. So I don’t really think I’m mistaken.
Can you tell me exactly what you think these people are doing to undermine you?

It’s mostly subtle things. Like after that commission, certain people in the ensemble started making schedule changes that would put me at a disadvantage, or they’d change seating in ways that made it harder for my work to come across properly.

And then in rehearsals there are these small comments—nothing they’d admit to if you asked them directly—but they land in a way that undercuts me or makes people question what I’m doing. When I bring it up, they’ll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it, but it’s been going on so long that I don’t think it’s just coincidence.
Has anyone else independently agreed that these ensemble members were trying to undermine you?

Not really independently, no. A couple of people have said the changes seemed odd, or that a comment in rehearsal felt pointed, but nobody has come out and said, “Yes, they’re trying to undermine you.”

That’s part of what makes it frustrating. They keep it subtle enough that other people can explain it away. But for me, after almost two years of the same kinds of schedule changes, seating decisions, and little comments after the commission, it feels too consistent to ignore.
Do you think these schedule changes and comments could be coincidences rather than deliberate attempts to undermine you?

I’ve tried to think of it that way, honestly. One schedule change could be a coincidence, or one comment in rehearsal could just be nothing.

But after almost two years, and especially since that commission, it’s hard for me to see it as random. It’s the same few things over and over—schedule changes, seating choices, little remarks that seem aimed at making my work look weaker. Even when they show me emails or notes explaining it, I still feel pretty certain there’s something deliberate behind it.
